To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

WISP3 protein is secreted into breast cancer cell media and into the lumen of normal breast duct, and that once secreted, it is able to modulate IGF-IR/IRS-1/ERK-1/ER2 signaling pathways, and to inhibit the growth of IBC cells

WISP3 protein is secreted into conditioned media and into normal breast ducts, and that, once secreted, it modulates IGF-IR/IRS1/ERK signaling pathways in IBC cells, leading to inhibition of cellular growth.
WISP3 protein is secreted and it modulates the IGF-IGF-IR signaling pathway in IBC cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of secreted proteins in breast cancer.
the identification and characterization of WISP3, a novel tumor-suppressor protein, and its potential as a therapeutic agent for the treatment of IBC.
the identification and characterization of novel tumor suppressor genes in IBC and their molecular mechanisms of action.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
WISP3, a secreted protein, inhibits IGF signaling and growth in IBC.
WISP3 has growth- and anti-angiogenic functions in breast cancer and that it does so, at least in part, by inhibiting IGF signaling.
WISP3, a putatively secreted tumor-suppressing protein, is secreted and it is capable of modulating the IGF- signaling pathways and cellular behavior in IBC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
WISP3, a secreted tumor suppressor protein, modulates IGF-IR pathways and cellular growth.
WISP3, a secreted protein, modulates IGF-IR/IRS1/ERK-1/ 2 signaling pathways in SUM149 cells, leading to decreased cell growth.
WISP3 has a growth-inhibitory function in IBC cells and that this function may be related to the modulation of IGF signaling.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the loss of WISP3 in IBC tumors leads to an unopposed activation of IGF signaling, which may be one of the mechanisms that contributes to IBC aggressiveness.
WISP3 may be an important therapeutic target for the treatment of IBC.
WISP3, by modulating IGF-IR activity and downstream pathways, can function as a tumor suppressor in human IBC.
